verified_findings.detail: JWT_SECRET=dev-insecure-change-me (22 bytes, below RFC 7518 minimum). Forged admin JWT → full access to /admin/kyc, /admin/audit-logs, /admin/transactions, /admin/withdrawals, /admin/datasets, /admin/anomalies, /admin/account-deletions, /admin/compute/jobs, /admin/settlement-outbox
verified_findings.impact: Complete admin takeover. Attacker can view all users, approve/reject KYC, manage datasets, approve withdrawals, access audit logs.

verified_findings.detail: When Redis is unreachable, refresh-token revocation is silently skipped. A stolen/leaked refresh token can be endlessly replayed by killing Redis (or during any Redis outage).
verified_findings.impact: Session hijacking persistence. Logout is ineffective during Redis downtime.

verified_findings.detail: When Redis is unreachable, rate limiting is completely disabled. 25 consecutive login attempts all returned 401 (not 429) after Redis was stopped, vs. rate-limited to 10/min when Redis is up.
verified_findings.impact: Brute-force attacks unhindered during Redis outage. Account enumeration and credential stuffing become viable.

verified_findings.detail: GET /metrics returns full Prometheus metrics (Go runtime, HTTP latencies, DB pool stats) without authentication.
verified_findings.impact: Internal performance data, error rates, and traffic patterns exposed to anyone.

verified_findings.detail: GET /docs/openapi.yaml serves complete 59KB OpenAPI 3.0 spec including all admin routes, request/response schemas, and module structure.
verified_findings.impact: Complete attack surface blueprint for reconnaissance without any access.
Attacker knows they are in development mode, where dev routes (/dev/mark-paid, /compute/purchase) are active.

verified_findings.detail: POST /payments/dev/mark-paid and POST /datasets/:id/compute/purchase are mounted (devMode=true). With admin forged token, these could manipulate payment/compute state.
verified_findings.impact: Free payments and compute entitlements in dev mode.

verified_findings.detail: HMAC key is 22 bytes, below RFC 7518 Section 3.2 minimum of 32 bytes for HS256. pyjwt flagged InsecureKeyLengthWarning.
verified_findings.impact: Reduced brute-force resistance for the signing key.

verified_findings.detail: Two anomaly rules failed on startup: repeated_failure and bulk_modification with SQL error "syntax error at or near LIMIT".
verified_findings.impact: Some anomaly detection rules are non-functional.

exploit_chain.step2: Register account (no CAPTCHA, no email verification)
exploit_chain.step5: Forge admin JWT with role=admin → full system access
exploit_chain.step6: Kill Redis → replay refresh tokens endlessly
exploit_chain.step7: Kill Redis → brute-force logins without rate limit
